forces.title: Sustained Digital Infrastructure and AI Investment Bolsters Sector Strength
forces.description: The UK computers and telecoms sector benefits from ongoing public and private investment in digital infrastructure, AI, and skills development, through initiatives like the Digital and Technologies Sector Plan, AI Growth Zones, and TechFirst. This sustained investment underpins the sector's long-term strength and helps offset external pressures, driving growth and innovation in connectivity and AI adoption, directly supporting all sub-nodes of SE09.
forces.source_title: September 2026 UK Sector Snippets

forces.title: Elevated Data Centre Energy Costs Create Near-Term Sector Uncertainty
forces.description: The UK computers and telecoms sector faces uncertainty due to higher energy costs for data centres. As digital infrastructure, including AI-driven solutions, expands, the operational expenditure related to power consumption increases, impacting profitability and potentially delaying investment decisions. This cost pressure is a significant factor contributing to near-term uncertainty within the sector, particularly affecting the demand for network infrastructure from SE09 players.
forces.source_title: September 2026 UK Sector Snippets

forces.title: Semiconductor Shortages Threaten Shipments and Introduce Supply Chain Risks
forces.description: Semiconductor constraints continue to be a significant concern for the computers and telecoms sector, with shortages potentially reducing shipments by around 9%. This supply chain vulnerability, exacerbated by broader geopolitical pressures, limits production capacity and introduces volatility. Businesses in Telecom Network Equipment (IN090201) and those relying on computing hardware must manage these risks carefully to ensure operational continuity and mitigate potential negative impacts on growth.
forces.source_title: September 2026 UK Sector Snippets

forces.title: Increasing Cyber Attack Threat Poses Major Concern for Sector
forces.description: Cybersecurity remains a key concern for the UK computers and telecoms sector, following major attacks in 2025. The escalating threat of cyber risks introduces near-term uncertainty, requiring businesses to prioritize robust security measures. Effective management of these risks is crucial for protecting digital infrastructure, maintaining customer trust, and ensuring operational stability in an increasingly connected environment, directly impacting the resilience of Telecom Services (IG0901) and Internet Platforms (IG0903).
forces.source_title: September 2026 UK Sector Snippets

forces.title: Persistent Talent Shortages Challenge Sector Growth and Innovation
forces.description: The UK computers and telecoms sector faces ongoing challenges from talent shortages, which continue to hinder growth. While accelerating AI adoption and digital infrastructure investment provide long-term strength, the scarcity of a skilled workforce creates operational bottlenecks and can limit the pace of innovation. Businesses need to invest in workforce development and risk management strategies to mitigate this constraint, affecting the ability of all SE09 players to innovate and scale effectively.
forces.source_title: September 2026 UK Sector Snippets

forces.title: Reversal of AI Talent Drain Boosts UK's Innovation Ecosystem
forces.description: The UK is a global magnet for highly skilled AI talent, with a net inflow from the US in 2025. Anchored by institutions like Google DeepMind, this concentration creates powerful cluster effects, offering proximity to elite research and industry partners. This talent pool is critical for developing and scaling AI applications, directly benefiting the innovation and competitiveness of Internet Platforms and Digital Media companies (IG0903) within SE09, fostering advanced digital services and products.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

forces.title: Late-Stage AI Application Funding in Europe Outpaces US, Supports Scale-ups
forces.description: Europe's AI application ecosystem shows strong funding momentum, with average late-stage rounds reaching nearly €200 million in H1 2026, surpassing the US. This capital foundation supports sustainable scale-ups, enabling rapid growth for AI-driven companies. This influx of growth capital provides a significant tailwind for Internet Platforms and Digital Media (IG0903) that leverage AI for their services and products, facilitating innovation and market expansion.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

forces.title: AI Companies Adopt Hybrid Pricing, Tying Costs to Measurable Outcomes
forces.description: Leading AI companies are increasingly adopting hybrid commercial models, blending per-seat licensing with usage-, consumption-, or value-based pricing. This shift ties software costs directly to delivered results, meeting enterprise buyers' demand for measurable ROI. This structural change impacts how digital media and internet platforms (IG0903) develop and price their AI-powered services, favoring those that can clearly demonstrate value and efficiency, driving a focus on performance-based business models.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

forces.title: AI Automation Drives Internal Operational Efficiency Across European Enterprises
forces.description: European companies are increasingly using AI-assisted automation to redesign internal functions (finance, support, delivery, internal tooling). This strategy maximizes workforce efficiency, decoupling revenue growth from linear headcount expansion, which is particularly incentivized by European employment laws. This structural shift towards AI-enabled operations offers significant productivity gains for Communication Services companies, especially Internet Platforms (IG0903) and Telecom Services (IG0901), by optimizing their internal processes and resource allocation.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

forces.title: AI Agents Reshaping Telco Opex with a 70:30 Legacy-to-AI Cost Ratio
forces.description: Telecom operators are undergoing a significant structural shift towards an 'agentic operating model' within the next 3-5 years. AI agents are set to automate or augment work across customer care, network operations, software engineering, and enterprise functions, leading to a new cost structure where AI agent and token costs comprise 20-30% of total operating expenditures. This fundamentally redefines how telcos manage their operations and costs, demanding a strategic overhaul in Telecom Services (IG0901).
forces.source_title: AI in Telecom: The Opex Reckoning

forces.title: Unmanaged AI Adoption Risks Increasing Telco Operating Expenses Without Productivity Gains
forces.description: Telcos face a critical risk of 'cost-creep' by simply adding AI token costs to their existing heavy legacy operating cost base without achieving proportional productivity, customer experience, or growth gains. This risk is amplified by factors like cheaper AI models leading to bigger bills, bolting AI onto legacy processes, and mistaking demos for actual transformation, making proactive cost management essential to avoid detrimental financial outcomes for Telecom Services (IG0901).
forces.source_title: AI in Telecom: The Opex Reckoning

forces.title: Legacy Systems and Regulatory Constraints Hinder Telco AI Modernization
forces.description: The transition to AI-powered operations is more challenging for the telecom industry than for digital-native companies. Telcos must modernize while simultaneously managing complex legacy operations, business support systems, large outsourced workforces, and intricate vendor relationships, all while complying with regulatory and labor constraints. These inherent complexities make achieving AI-driven productivity gains significantly more difficult for Telecom Services (IG0901), slowing the pace of transformation.
forces.source_title: AI in Telecom: The Opex Reckoning

forces.title: Rapid Data Centre Growth Fuels Electricity Demand, Creating Infrastructure Opportunities
forces.description: Rapid growth in data centre build-outs is playing a major role in driving electricity demand, with data centres alone accounting for roughly half of the US's electricity demand growth. These facilities consume significantly more electricity than standard commercial buildings. While this primarily impacts Utilities (SE10), it also creates significant demand for robust power infrastructure and connectivity, presenting an upside driver for Telecom Services (IG0901) and Telecom Equipment & Infrastructure (IG0902) to support these power-hungry digital hubs.
forces.source_title: Economic Report 2026

forces.title: AI Redesigning Product Development Life Cycles for Efficiency
forces.description: Outperforming software organizations are achieving significant impact by integrating AI into the Product Development Life Cycle (PDLC), with leading teams exceeding twofold productivity gains. This involves reimagining end-to-end processes, changing team structures to focus on human judgment, building verification systems, and investing in upskilling. This structural change influences how Internet Platforms and Digital Media companies (IG0903) develop and scale their products, leading to substantial efficiency improvements and faster innovation.
forces.source_title: Beyond the copilot: Scaling the agentic product development life cycle

forces.title: Managing AI Spend at Scale Poses Significant Challenge for Enterprises
forces.description: The growing availability and adoption of AI models (proprietary, open-weight) introduce significant complexity to enterprise AI economics. Organizations face challenges in governing when, where, and how AI capabilities are consumed, leading to hidden costs from failed requests, content bloat, and model proliferation. Without robust AI FinOps capabilities and governance, scaling AI risks substantial resource expenditure without proportionate returns, impacting profitability for AI-intensive sectors like Internet Platforms (IG0903).
forces.source_title: The cost of intelligence: How CIOs can manage AI demand at scale

forces.title: AI Sourcing Evolves Beyond Buy-vs-Build to Flexible Multi-Model Strategies
forces.description: The traditional buy-versus-build question for AI capabilities is no longer sufficient. Organizations must now continuously evaluate the best mix of buying, building, hosting, routing, and switching between various AI models and deployment options (proprietary, open-weight, enterprise-hosted, edge) based on performance, cost, risk, and business value. This structural shift demands flexible architectures and sourcing strategies from Communication Services companies integrating AI.
forces.source_title: The cost of intelligence: How CIOs can manage AI demand at scale

forces.title: AI-Driven Valuations Questioned Amidst High Deal Activity in Tech Sector
forces.description: Despite leading in M&A deal value, the broader technology, media, and telecommunications sector faces low sentiment due to questioning of AI-driven valuations and the capital cycle's sustainability. This uncertainty is particularly strong in business models highly exposed to AI disruption, such as Software-as-a-Service (SaaS). This poses a key risk for Internet Platforms & Digital Media (IG0903) in terms of fundraising, M&A, and investor confidence, demanding rigorous diligence for M&A activity.
forces.source_title: Mid-2026 M&A Insights: AI Drives a Recovery, but Questions Remain

forces.title: AI Investment Bifurcates Valuations: Infrastructure High, Application Layers Correcting
forces.description: The AI ecosystem exhibits a defining valuation bifurcation: infrastructure-layer assets (data centers, computing, power) command extraordinary valuations due to visible demand, while application-layer companies are experiencing valuation corrections. This structural change impacts investment flows and M&A strategies within Communication Services, potentially directing more capital towards underlying telecom infrastructure (IG0902) supporting AI, while Internet Platforms & Digital Media (IG0903) face stricter valuation scrutiny, requiring buyers to distinguish genuine capabilities.
forces.source_title: Mid-2026 M&A Insights: AI Drives a Recovery, but Questions Remain

forces.title: AI Projected to Significantly Boost UK Labor Productivity and GDP
forces.description: AI is forecast to lift UK labor productivity by +3.4% and contribute +1.7% to total GDP over the next decade, positioning the UK as one of Europe's strongest beneficiaries. This widespread economic enhancement from AI investment creates a significant upside driver for all sectors, including Communication Services (SE09), by stimulating demand for digital infrastructure, connectivity, and advanced digital platforms and services across the economy.
forces.source_title: Q3 UK economic outlook: Growth holds, inflation bites

forces.title: AI Investment Cushions Global Economy Against Geopolitical and Trade Disruptions
forces.description: Globally, investment in AI is acting as a strong economic cushion, helping the global economy navigate disruptions caused by geopolitical conflicts and rising trade tensions. This significant influx of capital and focus on technological advancement supports overall economic resilience, providing a cyclical tailwind that benefits technology-dependent sectors like Communication Services (SE09) by driving innovation, demand, and operational efficiencies, thereby mitigating broader macroeconomic headwinds.
forces.source_title: Q3 UK economic outlook: Growth holds, inflation bites

forces.title: London's High Data Center Energy Costs Challenge UK's AI Competitiveness
forces.description: The levelized cost of AI colocation data center energy in London is close to $380 per MWh, significantly higher than in some other regions. Energy costs account for a large portion of operational expenses for data centers, which are critical components of digital infrastructure. This high cost poses a headwind for the UK's attractiveness for AI infrastructure investment, potentially impacting the expansion of underlying network infrastructure and services provided by SE09.
forces.source_title: Colocation data centers: The infrastructure race behind AI

forces.title: UK's Deep Digital Ecosystem Attracts Networked AI Data Center Investment
forces.description: Despite higher energy costs, markets like the United Kingdom attract AI data center investment due to their status as 'demand-led hubs with deep digital ecosystems' and the requirement for fiber connectivity and proximity to major users. This positioning creates an upside driver for Telecom Services (IG0901) and Telecom Equipment & Infrastructure (IG0902) as data centers require advanced, high-bandwidth network infrastructure and services to function optimally, reinforcing the UK's role in digital economy.
forces.source_title: Colocation data centers: The infrastructure race behind AI

forces.title: Evolution of Gen AI to Autonomous 'Digital Workers'
forces.description: Generative AI is evolving from assistive tools to autonomous 'digital workers' capable of executing complex tasks with limited supervision, enabled by advances in reasoning models and agentic skills. This cognitive shift allows AI agents to apply domain-specific rules and enterprise know-how, moving beyond isolated tasks to autonomous workflow execution. This structural transformation presents opportunities for Communication Services to reinvent operations and service delivery with professional-grade AI capabilities.
forces.source_title: The symbiotic enterprise

forces.title: Enterprise Software Shifts to Outcome-Based Pricing for Industrial AI
forces.description: For asset-heavy industries like telecommunications, enterprise software companies are shifting from traditional seat-based licensing to outcome-based or asset-based pricing. This change, exemplified by IFS, reflects a move from paying for software access to paying for delivered outcomes (e.g., reduced unplanned downtime, lower operating costs) through AI-enabled digital workers. This structural transformation influences how Communication Services companies procure and value technology solutions, emphasizing measurable results and efficiency.
forces.source_title: The symbiotic enterprise

forces.title: Consumer Discovery and Attention Consolidating into AI-Driven Platforms
forces.description: Consumer discovery is rapidly shifting from the open web into AI-driven environments, with over 50% of Google searches including AI-generated overviews and 20-50% of traditional search traffic at risk by 2030. AI ranking now shapes the majority of consumer attention on integrated social media platforms like Instagram and TikTok. This structural shift consolidates user attention within AI-native platforms, significantly impacting Search, Social & Content Platforms (IN090301) and Digital Advertising (IN090302).
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: AI Agents Increasingly Drive Consumer Purchase Decisions and E-commerce Transactions
forces.description: AI is increasingly mediating consumer purchase decisions, with shopping agents and AI assistants ranking products, comparing alternatives, and completing transactions. Up to 35% of e-commerce transactions could be initiated, influenced, or completed through AI-native experiences. This structural shift moves advertising value towards players that can shape automated recommendations and selections, fundamentally altering the role of Digital Advertising & Ad Tech (IN090302) and Search, Social & Content Platforms (IN090301).
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Advertisers Anticipate Increased Media Spend and Higher ROAS from AI Adoption
forces.description: Three-quarters of advertisers surveyed expect their total media spend to increase in the next 12 months, fueled by new AI use cases and anticipated Return on Ad Spend (ROAS) gains. One-third of advertisers believe AI will drive at least a 10% increase in ROAS. This strong advertiser confidence and increased investment represent a significant tailwind for Internet Platforms & Digital Media (IG0903), driving revenue growth for ad-driven businesses by enhancing the effectiveness and scope of digital campaigns.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: AI-Native Buying Agents Threaten Traditional Ad Tech Intermediaries and Middleware
forces.description: The ad tech middle layer is experiencing significant compression as AI-native buying agents replicate cross-platform optimization within single workflows, potentially eliminating key use cases for supply-side platforms, exchanges, traditional demand-side platforms, and undifferentiated middleware. As AI automates buying, optimization, and measurement, intermediation layers built on cross-platform arbitrage face reduced relevance, posing a key risk for many Digital Advertising & Ad Tech (IN090302) players who rely on these traditional models.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: AI Accelerates Decline of Open Web Economics, Threatening Traditional Publishers
forces.description: AI is accelerating the erosion of open web economics, driven by declining traditional search traffic and increased consumer comfort with AI-generated answers. Click-driven, scale-dependent publishing and long-tail, SEO-dependent sites with limited subscription models are most exposed, facing potentially unviable business models. This poses a significant key risk for content providers that rely on traditional advertising and traffic, pushing them towards content licensing to AI platforms or premium coalitions, shifting the value away from the traditional open web.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

forces.title: Ad Tech Opportunity in Neutral, Cross-Platform Infrastructure and Governance
forces.description: Despite compression in the ad tech middle, opportunities exist for specialized ad tech players to serve as connective tissue across walled gardens and AI platforms. This involves investing in neutral, cross-platform identity, measurement, and AI performance audit services. As trust and governance become competitive differentiators, providing unbiased validation and testing platforms presents a defensible position and an upside driver for Digital Advertising & Ad Tech (IN090302) to maintain relevance by offering essential, independent solutions.
forces.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

viewpoints.title: UK Computers & Telecoms Sector Resilient Amidst External Pressures and Strong Fundamentals
viewpoints.description: The UK computers and telecoms sector demonstrates resilience, effectively navigating ongoing geopolitical, energy, and supply-chain pressures. This stability is underpinned by sustained public and private investment in critical areas such as AI, digital infrastructure, and skills development, through key initiatives like the Digital and Technologies Sector Plan. Accelerating AI adoption further contributes to the sector's long-term strength. However, the outlook is tempered by near-term uncertainties arising from higher data-centre energy costs, persistent semiconductor constraints, and escalating cyber risks following major attacks in 2025. Businesses are advised to manage these external challenges carefully while leveraging growth opportunities in connectivity and AI, maintaining prudent credit assessment. Overall, sector fundamentals remain strong, with a relatively low risk level (2).

viewpoints.title: Europe's AI Application Momentum Driven by Talent, Funding, and Innovative Models
viewpoints.description: Europe is experiencing strong momentum in AI applications, driven by a net inflow of AI professionals, a thriving university venture-building ecosystem, and increasing late-stage funding that now outpaces the US. This environment fosters the development and scaling of workflow-specific AI, particularly benefiting enterprise-grade, industry-embedded models. The region is adapting innovative, value-based commercial models and leveraging AI for internal operational efficiency, supporting the growth of digital platforms and services, which directly influences the Internet Platforms and Digital Media sub-sector (IG0903).
viewpoints.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

viewpoints.title: Telcos Face Critical AI-Driven Opex Shift Requiring Proactive Cost Management
viewpoints.description: Telecom operators are on the brink of a major shift in operating cost structures over the next 3-5 years, as AI agents become embedded in customer care, network operations, software engineering, and enterprise functions. While AI offers significant value, telcos face unique challenges due to legacy systems, large outsourced workforces, and regulatory constraints. Without proactive management, scaling AI risks merely adding token costs to existing legacy expenses, leading to higher operating expenditures without proportional productivity gains. This necessitates careful strategic action from players in Telecom Services (IG0901).
viewpoints.source_title: AI in Telecom: The Opex Reckoning

viewpoints.title: Tech, Media & Telecom M&A Exhibits Paradoxical Low Sentiment Despite High Deal Value
viewpoints.description: The Technology, Media, and Telecommunications sector (which includes SE09) shows the lowest M&A sentiment (52) despite leading in first-half deal value. This paradox reflects buyer caution regarding AI-driven valuations and the capital cycle's sustainability, especially for SaaS models highly exposed to AI disruption. A bifurcation is observed, with infrastructure assets commanding high valuations, while application-layer companies' valuations are correcting. M&A activity is expected to shift towards application-layer acquisitions, demanding rigorous diligence to differentiate genuine capabilities from AI enthusiasm, directly impacting Internet Platforms & Digital Media (IG0903).
viewpoints.source_title: Mid-2026 M&A Insights: AI Drives a Recovery, but Questions Remain

viewpoints.title: AI Investment Acts as Strong Economic Cushion Amidst Global Disruptions
viewpoints.description: Despite global economic disruptions from geopolitical conflicts and trade tensions, AI investment is serving as a strong economic cushion for the UK. AI is projected to boost UK labor productivity by +3.4% and total GDP by +1.7% over the next decade, one of Europe's strongest gains. While a moderate negative employment effect (-1.1%) from displacement is expected, the overall impact of AI investment is positive, providing broad support for technology-intensive sectors like Communication Services. This drives demand for digital infrastructure and advanced platforms.
viewpoints.source_title: Q3 UK economic outlook: Growth holds, inflation bites

viewpoints.title: Telecom and Media Sectors Lead AI Adoption Due to Digital Maturity and Data Richness
viewpoints.description: The telecommunications and media sectors are among the fastest to scale AI solutions, benefiting from digitally mature operations, rich structured data, and service-heavy revenue models. These industries built integrated data platforms and standardized processes early, providing a strong foundation for deploying vertical AI agents more quickly and cost-effectively. This leadership in AI adoption positions Communication Services for significant value creation, as evidenced by hundreds of identified generative AI use cases with substantial Net Present Value, indicating a strong future for AI integration within the sector.

viewpoints.title: Agentic AI Reshaping Advertising Economy, Consolidating Value in Integrated Platforms
viewpoints.description: Agentic AI is fundamentally reshaping the advertising economy, with value shifting towards platforms that can influence what consumers see, select, and purchase. AI is driving consumer discovery into AI-driven environments, increasingly mediating purchase decisions, and concentrating value within integrated platforms that bundle data, measurement, and transactions. While AI is expected to increase total media spend and ROAS, it also compresses the ad tech middle and threatens traditional publishers, creating a bifurcated market that favors AI-native platforms within Internet Platforms & Digital Media (IG0903).
viewpoints.source_title: The agentic advertising economy: From attention to action

viewpoints.title: Strategic GenAI Partnerships Crucial for Driving ROI Across Enterprise Journeys
viewpoints.description: Organizations are increasingly relying on strategic partnerships to achieve GenAI objectives, with 75% viewing partners as major ROI contributors and 85% planning expanded engagement. Over 90% leverage multiple partner types across their GenAI journey, expecting 3:1 or better ROI within one to two years. Effective partner selection, matching capabilities to specific phases from exploration to autonomous system design, is critical for unlocking operational efficiency, productivity gains, and revenue growth across various enterprise functions, including those in Communication Services, as they implement AI strategies.
viewpoints.source_title: How CTOs Can Choose the Right GenAI Partners at the Right Time

demand_drivers.driver: Fiber Connectivity and Proximity to Major Users
demand_drivers.description: AI data centers are highly networked assets, requiring robust fiber connectivity and close proximity to major users, which explains why markets like the United Kingdom, despite higher energy costs, continue to attract investment. This drives demand for high-capacity telecom services.

pnl_drivers.description: The high levelized cost of data center energy in London ($380/MWh) significantly increases operating expenses for data center infrastructure, impacting the profitability of digital infrastructure providers. This can influence investment decisions for new facilities and the associated demand for network equipment.

new_opportunities.description: The strong demand for data centers, particularly in 'demand-led hubs with deep digital ecosystems' like the UK, presents an opportunity for companies in Telecom Services and Telecom Equipment & Infrastructure to develop and provide advanced fiber connectivity and network solutions to support these critical digital hubs.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Investment in Fiber Connectivity and Digital Infrastructure

market_sizing.methodology: Levelized cost of data center energy (LCOE) for a 100-megawatt Tier 3-equivalent AI data center in London, calculated over a 20-year lifetime including 3 years of construction. Excludes taxes, subsidies, and externalities. Energy costs are identified as a primary driver of cost variation. The methodology leverages McKinsey's data center industry work, MGI's Economics Research team's proprietary databases for input costs, and McKinsey's Value Intelligence platform for capital costs.
market_sizing.source_title: Colocation data centers: The infrastructure race behind AI

demand_drivers.description: The increasing adoption and scaling of AI workloads, both for training large models and for running inference applications, is the primary driver behind the massive growth in data center power demand. This widespread integration of AI across industries fuels the need for expanded digital infrastructure.

new_opportunities.description: The monumental forecast for AI data center power demand creates a substantial new opportunity for companies in Telecom Services (IG0901) and Telecom Equipment & Infrastructure (IG0902). These data centers require advanced, high-bandwidth fiber optic networks and robust networking equipment to support their immense processing and data transfer needs.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Deployment of High-Capacity Fiber Connectivity and Network Equipment

market_sizing.methodology: Global forecast for AI data center power demand. AI training demand is projected to rise from 31 GW to 62 GW by 2030, and AI inference demand is expected to increase from 31 GW to 93 GW by 2030. The total power demand is calculated by summing the projected training and inference demands for that year.
market_sizing.source_title: Colocation data centers: The infrastructure race behind AI

demand_drivers.driver: Digitally Mature Operations and Rich Data
demand_drivers.description: The telecommunications and media sectors possess digitally mature operations and rich structured data, enabling them to rapidly identify and scale AI solutions across various functions, generating significant value from generative AI use cases.

new_opportunities.description: Over 250 generative AI use cases have been identified across IT, knowledge management, marketing and sales, service operations, software engineering, and product development within a European media and telecommunications company. These applications offer significant potential for productivity gains, revenue growth, and cost optimization for Communication Services firms.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Generative AI Use Cases Across Multiple Functions

market_sizing.methodology: Five-year Net Present Value (NPV) calculation for over 250 generative AI use cases identified across a European media and telecommunications company. The assessment included economic value, technical feasibility, and risk to prioritize viable cases for a realistic roadmap.
